topic: Internet Stories ep.7: the Oct 4 2021 Facebook outage. A command during routine maintenance (meant to check backbone capacity) cut every link between Facebook's data centres; its DNS servers withdrew their routes so the 'internet's phone book' had no answer and Facebook/Instagram/WhatsApp didn't exist to phones; staff reportedly couldn't get into buildings with badges (NYT via Wikipedia); engineers went to the data centres in person; ~6 hours. Lesson: social media is rented land, your website is land you own.
caption:
Facebook once deleted itself from the internet. By accident. 😳

For about 6 hours in 2021, Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp vanished worldwide. If your business only lives on Instagram, that's 6 hours where customers can't find you.

If Instagram went down tomorrow, could customers still find you? Tell me in the comments 👇

topic: Internet Stories ep.8: the first web banner ad. AT&T on HotWired (Wired magazine's website), October 1994: 'Have you ever clicked your mouse right here? You will.' About 44% clicked (agency's recalled figure). HotWired sold page space like a magazine to pay writers; a spot reportedly cost $30,000 for 3 months. It led to a page of art museum sites, not a sales pitch. Today banner ads get clicked by well under 1 in 100; banner blindness means flashy boxes get skipped, so keep key website info clear and plain.

caption:

topic: Why your website is slow: 5 usual suspects. Photos straight off the phone (resize ~2000px + compress), autoplay background video on the homepage, forgotten plugins loading code on every page, bolt-on extras from other companies' servers (chat, pop-up, Instagram feed, tracking codes), overseas hosting (host in Australia or use a CDN). Cover stat: Google 2016 research, 53% of mobile visits abandoned over 3 s. Last slide: test at pagespeed.web.dev. Made-up business Kestrel Plumbing, Wollongong. New light 'warm grey + inset photo card + navy number' look.
caption:
Your website isn't broken. It's stuck in traffic. 🚗
